summary_plain: This ground investigation analyzed data to understand why soot formation differs so much between normal gravity and microgravity. By combining computer simulations with experimental image analysis, researchers studied how flames behave in different gravity environments. This work helps improve fire safety and combustion technologies for spacecraft and Earth.
summary_expert: The documents provided describe the objectives and design only, as no experimental table or quantitative test results are given. The investigation analyzed gas fuels through computational and experimental methods, utilizing over 1600 raw DSLR images from the Smoke Point in Coflow Experiment (SPICE) data. Approach components included color-ratio pyrometry, absolute light calibration, and coupled flow-species-soot simulations incorporating radiation re-absorption and discrete-sectional aggregate formation for Yale and ACME burner configurations under normal and microgravity conditions.

key_findings.text: The investigation hypothesized that microgravity conditions would produce longer, more diffuse flames with lower temperatures and increased soot concentrations compared to normal gravity.
The study analyzed over 1600 raw DSLR images and incorporated advanced soot models to derive temperature distributions and soot volume fractions from SPICE data.

earth_applications: inform the design of cleaner energy and industrial systems
